title: ICE Officer Shoots Man in Austin, Sparking Protests and Demands for Local Oversight
snippet: A federal immigration agent shot a 28-year-old Venezuelan national during a traffic stop in North Austin, prompting community protests and calls from city officials for an independent investigation.
content:
A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer shot and wounded a 28-year-old man during a Sunday traffic stop in North Austin, triggering immediate public outrage and prompt demands from local officials for a transparent, third-party investigation.

The victim, identified by his family's attorney as Venezuelan national Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, sustained a single gunshot wound to the torso. He was transported to a local hospital in serious but stable condition before being quietly transferred directly into ICE custody Sunday evening—a move his attorney said occurred without notifying his family.

Local Authorities Push for Independent Inquiry

Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis clarified during a news conference that municipal police officers were not involved in the operation or the shooting. Austin Mayor Kirk Watson insisted that local authorities must be included in the oversight process to guarantee credibility.

"Austin residents have a right to feel safe in their city," Watson stated, adding that it would be inappropriate for federal agents to self-investigate the shooting. The Travis County District Attorney's Office similarly called on federal authorities to grant local prosecutors full access to the evidence.

U.S. Representative Greg Casar, whose district includes parts of Austin, criticized the federal action and called for an end to aggressive enforcement tactics. "It is awful that this horror has come to our doorstep," Casar told reporters. "For Austin to be safe, ICE should end its surge here."

Demonstrations Erupt at the Scene

Following the incident, roughly a hundred protesters gathered near an overpass on the city's north side, where a dark blue Toyota Corolla displaying bullet holes was parked before being towed. Tensions ran high as demonstrators chanted at police officers wearing tactical gear, while passing drivers honked in support of the protest.

The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, did not participate in the municipal press conference and has not released details regarding the circumstance of the shooting or the condition of the officer involved.

Widespread Enforcement Escalation

The shooting unfolds amid an aggressive nationwide push by ICE, which reported record arrest numbers over the summer. The heightened enforcement strategy has faced increasing scrutiny following several high-profile officer-involved shootings across the country, including recent fatal encounters in Texas, Maine, and Minnesota.
